what_went_wrong: The historical commit added pre-order/size-spec sub-schemas to MarketplacePost.js; those fields already exist in the current codebase (the commit already happened and is merged into HEAD), so investigating the present-day schema correctly shows 'everything needed is already there' -- the agent found accurate, relevant evidence but the task-as-framed ('extend the marketplace to support X') is not really an open question against an already-finished codebase.

Correctly found that getPosts() currently has no location/blood-type filter, then inferred a controller change would be required to add one. In the actual historical implementation, filtering was done client-side in the frontend against data already returned, so the controller never needed to change -- a reasonable but wrong architectural assumption despite accurate evidence.

marketplace.routes.js today already contains the full CRUD/management route set, because both the controller-only commit being evaluated AND the later commit that added the routes are already merged into current HEAD. Investigating the present state makes the routes and controller look like one inseparable unit, so the agent concluded both would be needed -- correct about current coupling, wrong about this specific historical commit's boundary.

getMyNotifications already implements correct recipient-based filtering today. The agent reasoned 'this is where per-user scoping logic lives, so this task touches it' -- true in general, but for this specific historical task the backend was already correct beforehand and the actual gap was purely in the frontend tray component (case 15) that didn't yet exist. Investigating a finished codebase made it hard to isolate which single file was the actual historical delta.

Correctly observed that the tray component doesn't implement its own recipient-filtering algorithm (it just renders an already-filtered API response). It then concluded the file 'doesn't need to be touched,' conflating 'doesn't implement the filtering logic' with 'doesn't need any changes' -- but building/fixing the user-facing tray experience is exactly the work that happens in this file, which is what the historical commit did.

The agent found no logical connection between auth.controller.js and blood-donor email notifications, which is accurate and defensible engineering reasoning. Ground truth reflects that an unrelated line (a domain-restriction check) was commented out in the same historical commit as the notification feature -- incidental bundling with no logical necessity, which no amount of correct current-state investigation could have predicted.

Correctly identified that RoommateCard.jsx has no form inputs while PostRoommateForm.jsx does, and took the task's literal word 'forms' to mean only the form file was in scope. Ground truth shows RoommateCard.jsx (the listing/display card) was in fact the file substantially changed -- the agent's own reasoning summary even flagged this as a live possibility ('RoommateCard could plausibly need a display tweak... but that's not what was requested') and still chose the literal reading.

Correctly found the widget currently has no search/ranking logic and that dedicated Python modules exist for preprocessing/reranking, then concluded no frontend changes were needed for a 'search relevance' task. Ground truth shows ChatbotWidget.jsx was in fact substantially rewritten (228 lines) in the same commit as the new Python modules -- the same frontend/backend task-framing bias seen in Conditions A/B/C persisted even with direct evidence in hand.
